problems.title: Sum of the array
problems.statement:
Given n integers, print their sum.

Values can be as large as 109 in absolute value, so the sum may not fit in a 32-bit integer.
problems.input_spec:
The first line contains n (1 ≤ n ≤ 2·105). The second line contains n integers.

Each value satisfies |ai| ≤ 109.

problems.title: Maximum and minimum
problems.statement:
Print the largest and the smallest of n integers, in one pass.

Careful: the numbers may all be negative.
problems.input_spec:
The first line contains n (1 ≤ n ≤ 2·105). The second line contains n integers.

|ai| ≤ 109.
problems.output_spec: Print the maximum and the minimum, separated by a space.

problems.title: Second largest distinct
problems.statement:
Print the second largest distinct value in the array. If all values are equal, print -1.

Try to do it in one pass without sorting.
problems.input_spec:
The first line contains n (1 ≤ n ≤ 2·105). The second line contains n integers.

0 ≤ ai ≤ 109.

problems.title: Insert at a position
problems.statement: Insert the value x so that it ends up at index p (0-based), shifting the later elements right. Print the resulting array.
problems.input_spec: First line n (1 ≤ n ≤ 105). Second line n integers. Third line p and x (0 ≤ p ≤ n).

problems.title: Delete at a position
problems.statement: Remove the element at index p (0-based), shifting the later elements left. Print the array, or EMPTY if nothing is left.
problems.input_spec: First line n (1 ≤ n ≤ 105). Second line n integers. Third line p (0 ≤ p < n).

problems.title: First occurrence
problems.statement: Print the index (0-based) of the first occurrence of x in the array, or -1 if it does not occur.
problems.input_spec: First line n (1 ≤ n ≤ 2·105). Second line n integers. Third line x.

problems.title: Answer occurrence queries
problems.statement:
Given an array and q queries, answer for each query value how many times it occurs in the array.

n and q can both be 2·105: scanning the array for every query is too slow. Values are small (1…100), so count them once.
problems.input_spec: Line 1: n. Line 2: n integers (1 ≤ ai ≤ 100). Line 3: q. Line 4: q query values (1 ≤ x ≤ 100).
problems.output_spec: q lines, the count for each query.

problems.title: Reverse the array
problems.statement: Reverse the array in place (two pointers) and print it.
problems.input_spec: The first line contains n (1 ≤ n ≤ 2·105). The second line contains n integers.

problems.title: Rotate right by k
problems.statement:
Rotate the array to the right by k positions: the last k elements move to the front, in order. k may be larger than n.

Aim for O(n) time and O(1) extra space (three reversals).
problems.input_spec: First line n and k (1 ≤ n ≤ 2·105, 0 ≤ k ≤ 1018). Second line n integers.

problems.title: Range sum queries
problems.statement:
Answer q queries: each gives l and r (0-based, inclusive) and asks for al + … + ar.

With n, q up to 2·105 you need O(1) per query.
problems.input_spec: Line 1: n q. Line 2: n integers (|ai| ≤ 109). Next q lines: l r (0 ≤ l ≤ r < n).

problems.title: Equilibrium index
problems.statement: An index i is an equilibrium index if the sum of the elements strictly left of i equals the sum strictly right of i (an empty side sums to 0). Print the smallest such index, or -1.
problems.input_spec:
The first line contains n (1 ≤ n ≤ 2·105). The second line contains n integers.

|ai| ≤ 104.

problems.title: Many range additions
problems.statement:
Apply m updates to the array; each adds v to every element with index in [l, r]. Print the final array.

Doing each update element by element is O(n·m) — use a difference array.
problems.input_spec: Line 1: n m (≤ 2·105). Line 2: n integers. Next m lines: l r v (0 ≤ l ≤ r < n, |v| ≤ 106).

problems.title: Pair with sum in a sorted array
problems.statement: The array is sorted in non-decreasing order. Is there a pair of different positions i < j with ai + aj = T? Print YES or NO.
problems.input_spec: First line n and T. Second line n sorted integers (|ai| ≤ 106).

problems.title: Remove duplicates from a sorted array
problems.statement: The array is sorted. Remove duplicates in place so each value appears once. Print the number of unique values, then the unique values in order.
problems.input_spec:
The first line contains n (1 ≤ n ≤ 2·105). The second line contains n integers.

The values are sorted in non-decreasing order.

problems.title: Move zeroes to the end
problems.statement: Move every 0 to the end of the array while keeping the relative order of the non-zero values. Print the result.
problems.input_spec: The first line contains n (1 ≤ n ≤ 2·105). The second line contains n integers.

problems.title: Best window of size k
problems.statement: Print the maximum sum of k consecutive elements.
problems.input_spec: First line n and k (1 ≤ k ≤ n ≤ 2·105). Second line n integers (|ai| ≤ 109).

problems.title: Shortest subarray with sum ≥ S
problems.statement: All values are positive. Print the length of the shortest contiguous subarray whose sum is at least S, or 0 if there is none.
problems.input_spec: First line n and S (1 ≤ n ≤ 2·105, 1 ≤ S ≤ 1015). Second line n integers (1 ≤ ai ≤ 109).

problems.title: Longest run of ones with k flips
problems.statement: The array contains only 0s and 1s. You may flip at most k zeroes to ones. Print the length of the longest block of consecutive ones you can get.
problems.input_spec: First line n and k (0 ≤ k ≤ n ≤ 2·105). Second line n values, each 0 or 1.

problems.title: Maximum subarray sum
problems.statement: Print the largest possible sum of a non-empty contiguous subarray.
problems.input_spec:
The first line contains n (1 ≤ n ≤ 2·105). The second line contains n integers.

|ai| ≤ 109.

problems.title: Transpose a matrix
problems.statement: Print the transpose of the R × C matrix: row i of the output is column i of the input.
problems.input_spec: First line R and C (1 ≤ R, C ≤ 500). Next R lines: C integers each.

problems.title: Spiral order
problems.statement: Print all elements of the matrix in clockwise spiral order, starting at the top-left corner.
problems.input_spec: First line R and C (1 ≤ R, C ≤ 500). Next R lines: C integers each.

problems.title: Rotate a square matrix
problems.statement:
Rotate the N × N matrix by 90° clockwise and print it.

Try to do it in place: transpose, then reverse every row.
problems.input_spec: First line N (1 ≤ N ≤ 500). Next N lines: N integers each (|a| ≤ 109).

problems.title: Leaders of an array
problems.statement:
An element is a leader if it is strictly greater than every element to its right. The last element is always a leader.

Print all leaders in their original left-to-right order. Aim for one pass.
problems.input_spec:
The first line contains n (1 ≤ n ≤ 2·105). The second line contains n integers.

|ai| ≤ 109.

problems.title: Majority element
problems.statement:
Print the value that appears more than n/2 times, or -1 if no value does.

Try Boyer–Moore voting: O(n) time, O(1) extra space — and remember to verify the candidate.
problems.input_spec:
The first line contains n (1 ≤ n ≤ 2·105). The second line contains n integers.

|ai| ≤ 109; the answer is never −1 as a value (ai ≠ −1).

problems.title: Sort 0s, 1s and 2s
problems.statement: The array contains only 0, 1 and 2. Sort it in one pass with O(1) extra space (Dutch national flag) and print it.
problems.input_spec:
The first line contains n (1 ≤ n ≤ 2·105). The second line contains n integers.

Each ai is 0, 1 or 2.

problems.title: Merge two sorted arrays
problems.statement: A and B are sorted in non-decreasing order. Print all n + m values in sorted order, in O(n + m) time.
problems.input_spec: First line n and m (1 ≤ n, m ≤ 2·105). Line 2: A. Line 3: B. (|values| ≤ 106.)
